exposure: trial of labor after two previous cesarean sections (TOLA2C)
cohort: 114 women with singleton pregnancies, absence of morphological abnormalities at ultrasonographic screening of the second trimester (or at any other stage of pregnancy), and two previous cesarean sections
finding: TOLA2C was associated with a success rate of 76.1%, a higher gestational age at birth, and a shorter hospital stay compared to elective repeated cesarean delivery, with no significant differences in the rate of low Apgar scores.
mod_finding: The percentage of successful TOLA2C in women with prior vaginal delivery was 92.8%.
gest_age: Higher in the TOLA2C group (specific values not reported)
